"De nacionalidad oriental, nacido en Montevideo, de cincuenta y seis [anos], de estado casado, y de profesion HACENDADO" - a landowner, which is the first statement of this family's standing anywhere in the archive. He died of pulmonary tuberculosis, certified by Dr Scremini. *** IT WAS HIDING UNDER A MISSPELLING: *** FamilySearch indexes him as Luis SERENA Lenguas, so every search under LERENA missed him, including a 1,502-row sweep of Montevideo Lerena deaths run the same morning. name: Ema Sixta LERENA Juanico
source: La Union marriage register act 90, 30 June 1913 - image read
note: *** Married JOSE PEDRO MASSERA (1866-1942), professor of philosophy at the Universidad de la Republica and later a Colorado senator; their son was the mathematician Jose Luis Massera. *** The witnesses at her wedding were her sister Maria and her brother-in-law Jaime Herrera - the couple of the 1886 act. Aged thirty-three on the act, so born about 1880; a findmypast index says 1876. She is the "Emma Liseta, 1876, father Luis, mother Julia" copied from a findmypast index on 9 September, four days before the family was identified. Named SIXTA for Sixta Lenguas Gonzalez, her mother's stepmother. *** HER BIRTH DATE IS NOW SETTLED AT 21 NOVEMBER 1876, not c.1880. *** Three independent records agree: the civil birth registration of 30 May 1903, the Uruguay Baptisms index, and her christening at the Catedral on 8 January 1881. The c.1880 came from her stated age at marriage in 1913, and ages at marriage are the weakest date in genealogy.

name: Dr. Don Candido JUANICO
source: Named as the bride's father and as a witness, Montevideo marriage act 258 (1864)
note: Father of Julia Juanico. Son of Francisco Juanico and Juliana Texeira. Stood as witness at his daughter's wedding in December 1864. *** HE MARRIED TWICE. *** Juliana Joaquina Gonzalez first - Julia, b.1842, is hers - and SIXTA LENGUAS second, by whom Sara, Zara Sista Emirena and Celia Juanico Lenguas, born 1866-1869. Note the second wife's surname: his daughter by the first married a Lerena LENGUAS. Justiniana Lenguas and Sixta Lenguas are very likely kin, which would mean these two families were already connected before 1864 - recorded as an observation, not a proved relationship.

name: Dona Juliana Joaquina GONZALEZ
source: Named as the bride's mother, Montevideo marriage act 258 (1864); and again as maternal grandmother in Montevideo baptism act 1720 (1886) - image read
note: Mother of Julia Juanico, and wife of Dr Candido Juanico. Published genealogy gives Candido's wife as SIXTA Lenguas Gonzalez, married 1857 - too late for a daughter marrying in 1864, so Juliana is an earlier wife. That is inference from dates. *** A THIRD ACT NOW NAMES HER, 13 September 2026: *** the baptism of her grandson Candido Jaime, San Francisco de Asis act No. 1720 of 6 July 1886, reads "maternos: Don Candido y Dona Juliana Gonzalez". Twenty-two years after the marriage act, the same parish still gives Julia's mother as Juliana Gonzalez. The published genealogy's SIXTA Lenguas Gonzalez is not what the registers say. *** AND THE TWO-WIVES INFERENCE IS CONFIRMED. *** Searching Candido Juanico as a father returns two distinct sets of children: Julia, by Juliana Joaquina Gonzalez, born 1842; and Sara, Zara Sista Emirena and Celia, all JUANICO LENGUAS, born 1866-1869 to SIXTA LENGUAS. A full generation apart. The published genealogy was right about the 1857 marriage and wrong to attach it to Julia.

name: Dona Justiniana LENGUAS Gonzalez
source: Named as the groom's mother, and a witness, in Montevideo marriage act 258 (1864)
note: Mother of the LERENA LENGUAS, and named as such in TWO acts read here: her son Luis Eugenio's marriage of 19 December 1864, at which she was also a witness, and her granddaughter Laura Adela's baptism of 1869, which calls her one of the "abuelos paternos". Her sister SIXTA LENGUAS GONZALEZ married Dr Candido Juanico - so the Lenguas married into both houses, and Sixta stood godmother to Laura Adela in 1869. That she was the second wife of Luis Lerena y Fernandez, and a daughter of Gen. Pedro Lenguas Grandal, is SECONDARY. *** SHE WAS ALIVE ON 24 DECEMBER 1901, AGED 79, and in the house where her son died. *** His death act No. 216 records her "de setenta y nueve anos, de profesion labores, domiciliada accidentalmente en la calle Suarez No. 25" - which puts her birth about 1822 and has her outliving Luis Eugenio.

name: Sancho LLERENA Aguilar
birthplace: Andalusia, Spain (the census says "Andaluzia"; CORDOBA comes only from a tree)
source: URUGUAY CENSUS 1726-1858, household 59 - image read; plus six indexed Uruguayan church and civil records
note: *** NOW PARTLY PRIMARY. *** The Uruguayan census records him at Calle San Juan, Montevideo, aged 45, birthplace "ANDALUZIA", with MARIA FERNANDEZ on the line below - image opened and read. Six further indexed records name the same wife and the same children while spelling him LLERENA, LERENA, SANCIO LLERENA, D. SANCHO LERENA and LORENA. So the alternation is in the RECORDS, not in a tree. That they are all one man is still an inference, and Cordoba specifically still rests on the tree alone. *** ORIGINALLY RECORDED AS SECONDARY. *** The founder of the Montevideo Lerenas on the tree's account: a soldier from Cordoba who married Maria Josefa Fernandez Tresguerras at Canelones, 8 January 1791. His name is spelled BOTH Lerena and Llerena across forty years of Uruguayan registers, and once - in 1828 - "Sancho de Llerena". The acts have NOT been opened here.

name: Candido Jaime LERENA Juanico
source: San Francisco de Asis, Ciudad Vieja, Montevideo, baptism act No. 1720, 6 July 1886 - IMAGE READ; image ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-Z9RS-F
note: *** A SEVENTH CHILD, and the best-documented of them all. *** Baptised 6 July 1886 at 21 months: "hijo legitimo de Don Luis Lerena Lenguas y de Dona Julia Juanico, orientales".
